newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS SIGN FREE AGENT SAFETY TURNER.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-RAIDERS SIGN FREE AGENT SAFETY TURNER.

text.p: The busy Oakland Raiders added another free agent to their roster Thursday by signing safety Eric Turner, a starter the last six seasons for the Cleveland Browns-turned-Baltimore Ravens.
Terms of the deal with Turner, who was released by the Ravens in February because of salary cap considerations, were not disclosed.
Earlier this off-season, the Raiders added quarterback Jeff George and Super Bowl MVP Desmond Howard to the team.

"I've prayed on this many a time for months that this would come true," said Turner. "The tradition...everything about the Raiders. They've got great defensive players here, great tradition, and I just wanted to be a part of that."
Turner was to receive a $1.3 million bonus if he was still on the Ravens roster on March 1. The team decided to release him after negotiations on a contract adjustment broke down.

"Talking to his teammates in Cleveland and Baltimore, probably the greatest tribute they gave was that everybody looks up to Eric Turner because of his work ethic," said Raiders coach Joe Bugel. "The three things they said, he's physically, mentally, spiritually tough."
The 28-year-old Turner was the second overall pick in the 1991 draft. He recorded five interceptions for the Ravens last year to increase his career total to 22.
Turner was named to his only Pro Bowl in 1994 after he recorded career highs with 167 tackles and nine interceptions for the Browns.
